item.title: Mechanically‐Driven Reconstruction of Lithium Metal for Stable All‐Solid‐State Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 Mechanical reconstruction via repeated folding/rolling transforms commercial Li from surface to bulk, creating an oxide-passivated surface and strong Li(200) texture. High-degree reconstruction homogenizes texture, synchronizes interfacial Li motion, suppresses voids and dendrites. This enables 79.3% retention after 1000 cycles, 7.4 mAh cm⁻² operation, and stable cycling below 0.5 MPa—a direct materials-level strategy for sulfide ASSBs.
🏷 lithium metal anode · all-solid-state battery · mechanical reconstruction · sulfide electrolyte · dendrite suppression

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Chemically etching Cu to form a sacrificial γ-CuCl interface creates micro-textured Cu with higher surface area; on reduction it releases Cl⁻ that tunes Zn²⁺ adsorption and suppresses hydrogen evolution. This synergy enables stable Zn plating at N/P = 1.0, with Zn//Cu cycling for 1654 h and Zn//MnO₂ cells reaching 53.5 mAh cm⁻³ and 70% retention over 500 cycles at 80 mA cm⁻²—a benchmark for material-limited Zn reversibility.

item.title: Breaking the Theoretical Capacity Limit of Fullerene Anode in Alkali‐Ion Batteries Through Two‐Dimensional Covalent Network Engineering

Advanced Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in pioneering metal-free 2D C60 covalent networks (tetragonal and hexagonal phases) as alkali-ion battery anodes, overcoming C60 aggregation and dissolution. Significance: TP-2D-C60 delivers 522 mAh g⁻¹, breaking C60's theoretical 446 mAh g⁻¹ limit, far exceeding pristine C60 (3.4 mAh g⁻¹), with demonstrated universality in sodium-ion batteries (309.9 mAh g⁻¹), rationalized by DFT binding-site and migration-barrier insights.

item.title: Decoupling proton transport from vanadium-ion crossover through filler-directed ionic domain engineering in blend membranes for vanadium redox flow batteries
item.description:

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using filler-directed ionic domain engineering in blend membranes to decouple proton transport from vanadium-ion crossover—a key trade-off limiting VRFB membranes. This approach enhances proton conductivity while suppressing vanadium crossover, improving membrane selectivity and long-term VRFB durability. Its significance is enabling higher efficiency and longer operational viability for grid-scale energy storage.
